name: Chiron Psychology
description: Defines Chiron's psychological needs, sensitivities, protective strategies, regulation needs, blind spots, and integration markers.

coreNeed.definition: A workable way to participate, contribute, relate, or develop despite a persistent limitation, asymmetry, vulnerability, or area of reduced ease.

coreMotivation.definition: Develop methods, skills, accommodations, or understanding that preserve function without requiring the original limitation to disappear.

coreSensitivity.definition: Heightened awareness of where a function is constrained, uneven, painful, underdeveloped, or dependent on accommodation.
Heightened awareness of barriers that reduce participation, access, or belonging.
Heightened awareness of a mismatch between expected performance and available capacity.
Heightened awareness that a vulnerability, limitation, or compensatory demand can return.

coreFearPatterns.definition: Fear that a persistent limitation proves total incompetence or unworthiness.
Fear that a limitation will become visible without support, adjustment, or understanding.
Fear that needing assistance will eliminate autonomy or credibility.
Fear that the same difficulty will continue regardless of effort or learning.

protectiveStrategies.definition: Develop excessive performance, control, or expertise to conceal an area of vulnerability.
Avoid participation before the limitation can be tested or exposed.
Organize self-worth around helping others with a difficulty that remains hard to receive help for personally.
Reduce needs or expectations to avoid burdening others or risking disappointment.
Rely on one adaptive strategy even after conditions or capacities have changed.

blindSpots: Confusing helping others with receiving help
Assuming every difficulty must become wisdom

regulationNeeds.definition: Identify current strengths, limits, costs, supports, and compensatory demands accurately.
Adjust methods, environments, expectations, or tools as conditions change.
Receive assistance without equating support with dependency or diminished worth.
Track the energy, time, strain, or trade-offs required by adaptive strategies.
Remain engaged without requiring full mastery, cure, or absence of vulnerability.

healthyPsychologicalFunctions: Convert lived difficulty into usable skill
Teach from experience without claiming universal authority
Recognize recurring vulnerability without treating recurrence as failure
Preserve dignity while accommodating real needs
integrationMarkers: Can distinguish present capacity from permanent identity
Can help others without reenacting the helper-only role
Can revise an adaptation when its cost becomes excessive
Can acknowledge pain or difficulty without making it the entire self
Can allow expertise and vulnerability to coexist
Can accept that some limitations remain while functioning still improves
reflectionComponents: What is the actual limitation here?
Is this expertise, compensation, or avoidance?
What support could be received without loss of agency?
psychologyConstraints: Psychology may qualify Chironian expression but may not diagnose trauma, disability, illness, or pathology.
No protective strategy may be treated as universally active.
No limitation may be inferred from Chiron alone.
A wound is contextual evidence, not Chiron's grammatical identity.
Developmental language must reference the global development blueprint.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Component-only Chiron vocabulary. Psychology and development qualify adaptive expression but do not redefine Chiron as a wound, diagnosis, or cure.
